content.title: About
content.content: The ham salad sandwich on wheat is a classic light lunch or snack. A layer of tender boiled ham, fresh lettuce, tomato and a light mayo‑based dressing is placed between two slices of whole‑grain wheat bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat bread provides slow‑release carbohydrates, helping maintain steady energy levels.
The ham used is often made from pork without added nitrites, making it a more natural option.
The salad component usually includes leaf lettuce and may add cucumber or radish for crunch.
Sandwiches became popular in the United States in the early 20th century with the rise of industrial bakeries.
The combination of ham and mayo offers a good balance of protein and fat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ham supplies high‑quality animal protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Whole‑grain wheat bread
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat bread provides dietary fiber, B‑vitamins and minerals that aid digestion.

items.title: Fresh vegetables
items.content: Lettuce and tomato add vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Balanced energy
items.content: The mix of carbs, protein and fat delivers sustained satiety.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham can be high in salt; people monitoring sodium intake should limit portion size.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some hams contain nitrites, which are undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free bread.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑rich due to mayo and bread fat; control serving size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. Add mustard, horseradish or avocado for flavor variation. For a lighter option, replace mayo with a yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. If the bread begins to dry, wrap it in cling film. Do not keep longer than 2 days to avoid ham spoilage.
